findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-75 — Deferred cancellation leaves a send window: a booking cancelled after the last cron run (but before the reminder fires) only gets `cancelled=true` in the DB; the cron's `scheduledDate <= now+1h` filter does not help because the reminder was already processed as non-cancelled, so the SendGrid scheduled send fires for a cancelled booking

[High/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:55-75 — The `for` loop aborts on the first SendGrid error (single outer try/catch), so one failing/poison reminder permanently blocks cancellation of all subsequent reminders on every cron run; additionally, the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises accumulated before the failure are never awaited, leaving floating promises with unhandled rejection paths

[Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177-186 — If `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` throws, the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` is skipped and the error is swallowed, leaving the SMS reminder scheduled in the DB with no `cancelled` flag and no retry mechanism; same pattern in `emailReminderManager.ts` where a failed prisma `update({ cancelled: true })` leaves nothing marking the reminder for the cron to cancel

[Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197-229 — The `immediateDelete` path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row; if the caller doesn't cascade-delete the booking/step (e.g., reschedule flow in `handleNewBooking.ts`), stale rows remain with `scheduled=true, cancelled=null`, and if the SendGrid cancel fails there is no DB marker so the cron will never retry the cancellation

[Medium/concurrency] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:484-494, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:484-494, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx — `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but called inside synchronous `forEach` with no `await`/`Promise.all`; the request handler can complete (and in serverless the process can be frozen/killed) before any cancellation or DB update executes

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964-976 — The `try/catch` around the `forEach` is ineffective because the async delete calls return unawaited promises, so rejections are not caught here; also, if `workflowReminders` was not included by the executed query branch, the `forEach` on `undefined` throws and reminders are silently not cancelled

[Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/components/WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 — Dropping `|| isSenderIdNeeded` from the condition hides the phone-number input and verification UI when a step only requires sender ID verification, breaking the sender-ID setup flow

[Medium/performance] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-58 — SendGrid cancel requests are issued sequentially (await inside the loop), one HTTP round-trip per reminder, and the `findMany` on `cancelled: true` has no `take` limit and no index on the new `cancelled` column, so scan cost grows with table size on every cron invocation

[Low/data] packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — `cancelled Boolean?` is nullable with no default, creating a tri-state (null/false/true) that all consumers must handle; `Boolean @default(false)` backfilled in the migration would be simpler and safer

[Low/doc_defect] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:901-963 — A large block (mostly commented-out code plus live code around the preview booking lookup) is re-indented with all leading whitespace stripped, mangling formatting of live code; looks like an accidental editor artifact and should be reverted

[Low/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:10 — Importing `Prisma`/`WorkflowReminder` from `@calcom/prisma/client` and typing the array as `Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>[]` leaks Prisma internals; `PrismaPromise<WorkflowReminder>[]` (or letting TS infer) is correct and less brittle

[Medium/test_gap] No tests cover the new deferred-cancellation lifecycle: `cancelled` flag semantics, the cron cancel/delete path in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `immediateDelete` behavior, or null-`referenceId` handling; the removed direct-delete assertions in existing flows are also unaccounted for

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-75 — Deferred cancellation leaves a send window: a booking cancelled after the last cron run (but before the reminder fires) only gets `cancelled=true` in the DB; the cron's `scheduledDate <= now+1h` filter does not help because the reminder was already processed as non-cancelled, so the SendGrid scheduled send fires for a cancelled booking

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce deferred cancellation for email reminders: most call sites now invoke `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`, and that function (non-immediate path) only does `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` and does **not** cancel the SendGrid scheduled send right away. Actual SendGrid cancellation + DB deletion is moved into `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only cancels `cancelled: true` reminders when that handler runs and only for `scheduledDate <= now + 1h`. This creates a timing/race window where a scheduled send could potentially fire before the cancellation job executes (depending on how/when `scheduleEmailReminders` is triggered). However, the finding’s claim that the `scheduledDate <= now+1h` filter “does not help because the reminder was already processed as non-cancelled” isn’t strictly supported by the diff—the job does target `cancelled: true` reminders and would still cancel previously scheduled sends if it runs in time. So it’s a real edge-case/design risk, but not a definitively verifiable bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:55-75 — The `for` loop aborts on the first SendGrid error (single outer try/catch), so one failing/poison reminder permanently blocks cancellation of all subsequent reminders on every cron run; additionally, the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises accumulated before the failure are never awaited, leaving floating promises with unhandled rejection paths

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the cancellation logic is wrapped in a single outer `try/catch` around a `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop. If `client.request(...)` throws for any one reminder, control jumps to the `catch` and the loop stops, so subsequent reminders in `remindersToCancel` are not processed on that run. Also, the code queues `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` operations into `workflowRemindersToDelete` but only awaits them after the loop; if an exception occurs mid-loop, the already-queued deletes are never awaited/executed, leaving the DB cleanup incomplete and state inconsistent with any already-performed SendGrid cancels.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177-186 — If `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` throws, the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` is skipped and the error is swallowed, leaving the SMS reminder scheduled in the DB with no `cancelled` flag and no retry mechanism; same pattern in `emailReminderManager.ts` where a failed prisma `update({ cancelled: true })` leaves nothing marking the reminder for the cron to cancel

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder wraps both `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` in the same `try`. If `twilio.cancelSMS` throws, execution jumps to `catch`, the Prisma delete is skipped, and the error is only logged—so the reminder row can remain in DB without any `cancelled` marking (the schema adds `cancelled`, but SMS path never sets it). Similarly in emailReminderManager.ts, the cancellation path for non-immediate deletes relies on `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true }})`; if that update throws, the `catch` only logs, leaving no DB flag for the later cancellation logic in scheduleEmailReminders.ts (which queries `cancelled: true`) to act on.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197-229 — The `immediateDelete` path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row; if the caller doesn't cascade-delete the booking/step (e.g., reschedule flow in `handleNewBooking.ts`), stale rows remain with `scheduled=true, cancelled=null`, and if the SendGrid cancel fails there is no DB marker so the cron will never retry the cancellation

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)`, the `immediateDelete` branch cancels the SendGrid batch and then `return`s without updating/deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row (no `cancelled=true`, no delete). The diff shows at least one caller where no cascade delete is evident: `handleNewBooking.ts` reschedule flow calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` and does not delete/update those reminders afterward. That leaves stale DB rows (e.g., still `scheduled=true`, `cancelled` unset) and also means the new cancellation retry logic in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (which only processes `cancelled: true`) will never pick them up if the SendGrid cancel fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964-976 — The `try/catch` around the `forEach` is ineffective because the async delete calls return unawaited promises, so rejections are not caught here; also, if `workflowReminders` was not included by the executed query branch, the `forEach` on `undefined` throws and reminders are silently not cancelled

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new cancellation logic wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` in a try/catch, but the calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` are async and are not awaited (and `forEach` doesn’t aggregate/await promises). As a result, any rejection from those async deletes will not be caught by the surrounding try/catch and can surface as unhandled promise rejections / silently fail to cancel before reschedule continues. The second point about `workflowReminders` being undefined is less verifiable from the diff because this PR also adds `workflowReminders: true` to the shown include, but the unawaited async/catch issue is directly shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/components/WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 — Dropping `|| isSenderIdNeeded` from the condition hides the phone-number input and verification UI when a step only requires sender ID verification, breaking the sender-ID setup flow

adjudication.rationale: In WorkflowStepContainer.tsx the render condition for the phone-number/verification block was changed from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to only `isPhoneNumberNeeded`. This means when `isSenderIdNeeded` is true but `isPhoneNumberNeeded` is false, the entire UI block (phone input + verification controls) will no longer render, which can break any flow that relied on showing this UI for sender-ID-only requirements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-58 — SendGrid cancel requests are issued sequentially (await inside the loop), one HTTP round-trip per reminder, and the `findMany` on `cancelled: true` has no `take` limit and no index on the new `cancelled` column, so scan cost grows with table size on every cron invocation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block does `const remindersToCancel = await prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})` with no `take`/pagination, so it can grow unbounded per cron run. It then iterates `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) ... }`, which issues SendGrid cancel requests sequentially (one await per reminder). The diff also shows the `cancelled` column being added via migration/schema without any index creation, making the `cancelled: true` filter potentially table-scan heavy as data grows. This is a concrete performance/scalability concern introduced by the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:10 — Importing `Prisma`/`WorkflowReminder` from `@calcom/prisma/client` and typing the array as `Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>[]` leaks Prisma internals; `PrismaPromise<WorkflowReminder>[]` (or letting TS infer) is correct and less brittle

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the diff explicitly adds `import { Prisma, WorkflowReminder } from "@calcom/prisma/client";` and types `workflowRemindersToDelete` as `Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>[]`. That type is a Prisma-generated internal client type; using `PrismaPromise<WorkflowReminder>[]` or relying on inference would be less brittle and avoid coupling to Prisma internals. This is a maintainability/typing concern rather than a functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No tests cover the new deferred-cancellation lifecycle: `cancelled` flag semantics, the cron cancel/delete path in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `immediateDelete` behavior, or null-`referenceId` handling; the removed direct-delete assertions in existing flows are also unaccounted for

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new deferred-cancellation lifecycle for workflow reminders: a new nullable `cancelled` column (migration + `schema.prisma`), changed semantics in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` (now updates `cancelled` vs immediate API cancel, and deletes locally when `referenceId` is null), new deletion behavior in `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` (always deletes DB record, cancels via Twilio only if `referenceId`), and a new periodic cancel+delete path in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that finds `cancelled: true` reminders within the next hour and cancels via API then deletes them. The PR diff does not add/modify any tests alongside these nontrivial behavioral changes, so a concrete, diff-grounded gap is that these new branches/flows are untested in this change set (even if tests might exist elsewhere).
